transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess what brings me in is, it’s probably a little silly, but if I even think there might be a bat or something flapping around in the stockroom at work, my heart just kind of jumps. I start sweating, and I feel like I need to get out of there right away. I know that might sound over the top, but it’s been hard to just shake off.
When you're in situations where you think there might be a bat nearby, do you ever feel like you're having a panic attack—like your heart races, you feel dizzy, or like you can't breathe?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it a panic attack exactly, but it does come on really fast. Like the second I think there might be a bat in the stockroom, my heart kind of jumps, I start sweating, and I just feel like I need to get out of there right then. It feels a little embarrassing saying it that way, but yeah, that’s pretty much what happens.
Do you find yourself avoiding going into the stockroom or other places where you think there might be bats, even if you don’t see one?

Yeah… I mean, not completely, like I still do my job, but I guess I’ve been kind of working around it. I’ve swapped out some closing shifts, and I’ll take the long way around the loading area if I can. And if I have to check the stairwell, I sort of make myself do it quickly, holding my phone, just… pretty scared the whole time. I know that probably sounds like a lot.
Have you ever avoided going into certain areas at work or elsewhere because you were afraid a bat might be there, even if the chances were low?

Yeah… I guess I have, a bit. I’ve been swapping out some closing shifts when I can, and I’ll take the longer way around the loading area, even though I know it’s probably not that likely anything’s there. And if I have to check the stairwell, I sort of rush through it with my phone in my hand, just feeling scared the whole time. I know that probably sounds kind of unnecessary, but… yeah.
How long has this fear of bats been bothering you, and does it cause you significant distress or interfere with your work or other parts of your life?

It’s been going on long enough that it’s… not just a one-time thing, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job, because I can, but it has started to affect work.

My manager has kind of noticed I keep trading out of closing duties, and that I’m not as reliable with the after-hours checks. He’s started asking if I can really handle the shift lead role. And that’s… honestly pretty upsetting, because I was hoping that would turn into a permanent management position. I feel kind of stupid that something like bats could mess with that, but yeah, it’s causing problems.
